text:
emma: quick flag from today's linkscan: a bunch of onboarding anchors in `docs/onboarding/quickstart.md` now 404 after a permalink change in the runtime guide. docs-bot shows a spike at ~09:12.

docs-bot: linkscan report: 7 dead anchors detected in `docs/onboarding/quickstart.md` (anchors: #runtime-config, #kv-cache, #batching). Report: scan-2026-03-22-0912.

emma: looks like the runtime guide refactor renamed some headings which broke anchor links. who touched the runtime permalinks recently? cc @raj since you worked on the docs refactor last sprint.

raj: yep that was my refactor. i moved the runtime guide from `runtime/guide.md` -> `runtime/serving.md` and changed some heading names to be clearer. didn't realize onboarding was using the old anchors. my bad.

nora: thanks for the ping. small plan: replace onboarding anchors to point at the new headings, or add shortlink redirects from old anchors to new ones. Which is preferable?

emma: prefer shortlink redirects so we don't have to touch a bunch of older guides referencing those anchors. also reduces churn in release notes. but we should update onboarding too if the heading moved contextually.

raj: fine with redirects. i'll create redirect entries in `docs/shortlinks/anchors/` mapping old anchors -> new `runtime/serving.md#...`. also will add a tiny note in the runtime file that the anchor was renamed for clarity.

emma: can we do a canary merge during US evening to avoid flapping staging linkchecks? last time link reorg tripped staging for ~20min.

nora: schedule looks clear tonight 01:00 UTC is low traffic. raj, can you target that window?

raj: yep scheduling for 01:00 UTC. PR will be small. i'll include both the redirect files and a changelog entry `internal: restore onboarding anchors via shortlink redirects`.

ci-bot: CI note: creating branch `docs/anchor-redirects-180124` and running link-checker pre-merge. Expect linkscan re-run on merge.

nora: one more ask: can we add a temporary exception in linkscan for shortlinks path so our pipeline doesn't create noise during the 10-min window when redirects propagate? it should be tolerant for 10 minutes after deploy.

emma: yes we should. file an infra ticket or i can add a short comment to the PR to pause linkscan. prefer to automate if we do this often.

raj: drafting PR now: https://git.example.com/redwood/docs/pulls/4301 (WIP). includes redirect yaml + small runtime heading note. i'll add instructions on how to rollback if anything weird happens.

nora: ping me when branch is pushed. i'll run a local link check against staging to validate redirects resolve as expected. also can check markdown lint for frontmatter.

emma: small reproduce curl incantation if folks want to test locally:

```bash
# simulate old anchor hitting shortlink redirect
curl -I "https://docs.internal.example.com/runtime/guide.md#runtime-config" \
  -H "Host: docs.internal.example.com" | grep -i location || true
```

raj: pushed branch and opened PR. CI shows linkcheck failed on current HEAD (expected). adding @nora for review and @emma for visibility.

ci-bot: PR #4301 status: checks started. linkscan will re-run post-merge.

nora: reviewing now. tiny nit: the redirect yaml needs a trailing slash escaped for the anchor mapping. i'll push a one-line fix to your branch if that's okay.

raj: please do, thanks. also added a rollback note in PR body and added `@docs` team mention.

emma: once merged i'll follow up with a brief note in the docs channel and mark this as resolved. thanks for the fast turnaround.

nora: merged during 01:02 UTC window. confirmed redirects live on staging. local linkcheck shows onboarding anchors resolved.

ci-bot: post-merge linkscan: 0 dead anchors in onboarding. all clear.

emma: lovely. follow-up: opening a tiny issue to add a unit to linkscan that detects anchor rename patterns and warns in PRs when a rename is likely to break external refs. not urgent but will help us catch these earlier.

raj: opened issue https://git.example.com/redwood/infrastructure/issues/212 - tag `infra` and `docs` for follow-up.

emma: thanks all, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
